summary: Hardin County, TX Texas Forest Service tower of 122 feet, announced as being erected in May 1962; listed as gone; no completion date or site description found.

facts.design: Planned all-metal structure, 122 feet tall, as announced in 1962
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal date or site description found

events.note: Announced in May 1962 as being erected by O. C. Braly Construction Company; no completion date given

evidence.supports: Announced May 1962 as being erected by the Texas Forest Service in Hardin County near Grayburg
evidence.quote: A Texas Forest Service fire lookout tower is being erected in Hardin County near Grayburg

evidence.supports: 122 foot height; builder O. C. Braly Construction Company of Overton, Texas
evidence.quote: This 122 foot tower is being built by the O. C. Braly, Construction Company of Overton, Texas
will be an all metal structure when completed.

evidence.supports: Fire supervisor Archie T. Nash for the Texas Forest Service
evidence.quote: Archie T. Nash, Fire supervisor for the Texas Forest Service announced today.

evidence.supports: Purpose: detection in southwest Hardin, north Jefferson and east Liberty counties
evidence.quote: This additional fire lookout tower will aid greatly to forest fire detection in Southwest Hardin, North Jefferson and East Liberty Counties,

evidence.supports: District would have 15 lookout towers with the addition
evidence.quote: With the addition of this tower, District No. 4 comprised of Tyler, Polk, Hardin and part of Jefferson County will have a total of 15 lookout towers distributed over this District.

evidence.supports: View of about 150,000 acres from one tower on a normal day
evidence.quote: From one of these towers on a normal day a person may look over approximately 150,000 acres of East Texas timberland.

evidence.supports: Clipping was from The Silsbee Bee
Index lists the Grayburg tower as a tower with status Gone
Grayburg is on SH 326, 18 miles west of Beaumont, extreme southern Hardin County
evidence.quote: Grayburg is on State Highway 326 eighteen miles west of Beaumont in extreme southern Hardin County.

evidence.supports: Grayburg founded in 1908 when a lumber company built a sawmill
evidence.quote: It was founded in 1908, when the Thompson-Ford Lumber Company built a sawmill on the newly constructed Beaumont, Sour Lake and Western Railway.

sources.title: Grayburg, TX
sources.publisher: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas Online

notes_for_editor: The 1962 clipping (reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page from The Silsbee Bee) says the tower was being erected; no completion or dedication date was found, so the event is recorded as an announcement with that caveat. Height of 122 feet matches the record's 37.2 m. No staffing, fire or removal detail was found in the sources read. Two WebSearch calls were used; the second turned up nothing new about this tower. TSHA is used only for town background. No photo found.
